analysis.title: Up and Adam
key_insights: The S&P 500 has been little changed since early August, but breadth has improved. The share of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day moving average rose to 65.7% from 22.5% at the start of October.

The median S&P 500 stock is up 9.9% YTD, versus 6.3% two weeks earlier. Lower oil prices and yields are supporting a rotation into value-oriented sectors. Raymond James sees the broadening as encouraging and supportive of the bull market.

The Treasury's Quarterly Refunding Announcement (8:30 AM ET) will be watched for changes in auction sizes and the mix of short- and long-term borrowing. Secretary Bessent's surprise August decision to increase liquidity buybacks has fueled speculation that Treasury could cut long-term issuance or eliminate the 20-year bond.
Budget deficits are at post-COVID highs, so investors are focused on how the government funds its borrowing and who absorbs the supply.

The midterms produced a blue wave at the high end of expectations. Democrats have flipped 25 House seats, enough for a strong majority, and hold a Senate majority of 54 seats after flipping Iowa, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Kansas and South Carolina. Alaska and Mississippi are too close to call.

State-level results may tighten data center regulation. Democrats retained California and flipped Georgia, Ohio and Texas, four of the top five states by number of data centers. Texas Gov. Abbott has already tightened rules, so the trend is bipartisan.

September JOLTS beat consensus, with job openings at 7.5m, the highest since May. Hiring improved and layoffs fell to a 1.5-year low. Openings strengthened in goods-producing industries, while services were mixed.
Raymond James expects October nonfarm payrolls to rise 70k, up from 29k in September, and views the labor market as healthy. ADP is due today and BLS payrolls on Friday.
